articles.title: Treasury Unveils Rules for Big Investor Homebuyers After Congress Set Limits
articles.summary: The Treasury Department released its long-awaited guidance on how it plans to constrain institutional investors in the housing market.
articles.body:
The Department of the Treasury released its long-awaited guidance on how it plans to restrict institutional investors in the housing market.

Treasury unveiled the proposed rule that establishes standards for large institutional investors in the housing market. It follows a January executive order from President Donald Trump meant to discourage investors from benefiting from federal assistance in home purchases.

That led to some large investors to pull back, Realtor.com found in its own data. Small investors tend to have a far larger presence in the housing market, and they have been less scarce in the meantime.

"Treasury is working to ensure American families and workers have a fair shot at purchasing homes in their communities by increasing housing supply and limiting large institutional investors' role in the market, while supporting a strong, stable housing market and avoiding unnecessary disruption," Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement.

The new rules help define what makes a large instututional investor and creates carve-outs to the rules. In particular, for renovate-to-rent businesses. Often these companies purchase homes that require more work than an average homebuyer can afford, and then flip them.

The rules also clarify proposed penalties against real estate investors, which could reach up to $1 million, or three times the purchase price of a property. The rules are open for public comment for 30 days.

Congress codified further limitations in the 21st Century Road to Housing Act , which became law in July. That bill targets investors who own more than 350 properties. After some wrangling , it excludes the build-to-rent industry .

Large investors are concentrated in some large markets where they account for a significant share of the housing stock.

As expected, the rules prevent investors who control 350 or more single-family homes from purchasing more, starting January 7, 2027. Home bought before the bill became law on July 11 don't have to be sold.

The new material in the proposed rule is mostly in the exceptions and carve-outs, Realtor.com economist Hannah Jones said. For build-to-rent properties, a home must be a new build that is bought within 18 months of its certificate of occupancy. And, it must be occupied by a renter, though the bill does not specify a set period for them to live there.

Treasury indicated it has a few open questions. It's asking for comment on whether it should add a minimum time for renters to be in a property to prevent investors from building, renting briefly and then quickly selling homes.

articles.title: SpaceX stock slips as tech trade tumbles
articles.summary: SpaceX stock slipped  in early trading Thursday, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain.
articles.body:
SpaceX ( SPCX ) stock slipped in early trading Thursday, giving back more than half of Wednesday's post-earnings gain.

Shares jumped 7.8% on Wednesday following SpaceX's upbeat third quarter results and AI commentary.

The stock is under pressure today along with the broader tech trade, following Meta ( META ) earnings and more headlines suggesting new strikes in the US/Israeli war with Iran.

As for SpaceX, it guided fourth quarter capital expenditures to $35 billion to $40 billion, up from $19.6 billion in the third quarter, as more compute capacity comes online. The company ended the quarter with $36.1 billion in debt.

"The earnings call served to amplify the enormous calls on capital that loom over the next few years," MoffettNathanson analyst Julie Zhu wrote in a note to clients.

"We are investment grade, have a very strong balance sheet, and there are a number of available pools of debt capital," SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said on the earnings call.

Then there's the merger talk. Musk said SpaceX and Tesla ( TSLA ) have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a tie-up, and that he is recused as a conflicted party. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said .

That endorsement created a "mess" for the process, a person with direct knowledge of the talks told Reuters . Insiders worry the resulting shareholder scrutiny could delay talks by several weeks.

Bloomberg separately reported that the companies are aiming to announce a deal in the first half of 2027.

On the flipside, Wall Street is now more bullish on SpaceX's prospects. JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth more than doubled his price target to $500 from $240, citing AI infrastructure growth. BofA raised its target to $275 from $235.

Barclays analyst Dan Levy flagged Tesla's annual meeting, which must be held by Dec. 6, as the likely venue for a shareholder vote. He added that a deal announced in late October or early November could push approval out six to 12 months.

articles.title: PHP security flaws trigger global scramble; CERT-In flags critical vulnerabilities
articles.summary: CERT-In warns of critical PHP flaws under active exploitation, prompting urgent global patching, millions of attack attempts, and precautionary service shutdowns.
articles.body: Bengaluru: It has been a difficult day for cybersecurity, with critical vulnerabilities in PHP triggering an urgent global patching effort, millions of reported hacking attempts, and precautionary shutdowns of some online services. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said the scale of the incident was unusual, remarking at an event in Cologne in Germany that he had not seen anything like it “in a long, long time”.The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) issued a critical-severity warning over two vulnerabilities in PHP, a widely used open-source scripting language that powers websites and web applications. The flaws could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute malicious code remotely, disclose memory and potentially compromise affected systems.In its advisory issued on Wednesday, CERT-In said reports had confirmed large-scale exploitation in the wild and urged organisations and individuals using affected versions to apply security updates urgently.Google Cloud executives Chris Betz, chief information security officer, and Raluca Ada Popa, head of Gemini Security at Google DeepMind, said PHP and cybersecurity firm Wiz Research disclosed the two vulnerabilities after research that used multiple AI models to identify and help remediate them.Google Cloud said its own infrastructure was not vulnerable, but warned that customers running PHP applications on the platform could be exposed. It urged customers to update their applications to patched PHP versions and redeploy them. Google is also rolling out updated serverless base images for supported PHP runtimes, with automatic updates available for certain services and configurations.The scale of the response has extended beyond India. “In the 10 hours before it was publicly announced, across the network we saw thousands of attempts to exploit it,” Cloudflare CEO Matthew Prince wrote in a post on X on Wednesday. Companies and govt agencies in several countries temporarily restricted access to some online services as a precaution while they worked to secure vulnerable systems. Cloudflare’s blog said it successfully deployed mitigations for all its customers after the PHP vulnerabilities were leaked before their official disclosure date. The company observed attack traffic targeting customers and tracked how attackers modified their payloads to try to bypass its security. “Approximately 75% of all internet runs on PHP or some framework based on PHP including Wordpress, Drupal, Laravel, Joomla and these vulnerabilities impact the default configuration of the same. articles.title: Costco plans warehouse in a new state as others await their first store
articles.summary: Despite how popular it is, Costco hasn’t opened warehouses in every state – yet.
articles.body:
(NEXSTAR) – It’s finally happening: Rhode Island is getting access to the $1.50 hot dog combo , rotisserie chickens , and warehouse shopping.

That’s right, Costco is planning its first-ever warehouse in Rhode Island. Helena Foulkes, a candidate for Rhode Island governor and a member of Costco’s board, confirmed the news to Nexstar’s WPRI on Thursday. The store is expected to open in Smithfield, just outside of Providence, in 2028, thwarting the need for Rhode Islanders to drive to Massachusetts to use their Costco membership.

Rhode Island was among the last uncharted territories for Costco . As of October 2026, only two other states, West Virginia and Wyoming, are still awaiting their inaugural Costco.

They may not have to wait much longer, however.

Back in March, CEO Ron Vachris said the company aims to open 30 or more warehouses annually over the next five to 10 years , echoing remarks from CFO Gary Millerchip. Roughly half would be new warehouses in the U.S., while the others would be worldwide. Vachris mentioned Mexico, Canada, Asia, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand as sites for future warehouses.

In September, Vachris shared that the bulk retailer expects to open 33 new warehouses in fiscal year 2027 , though five are considered “relocations.” While it’s not entirely clear where these new stores will be, Vachris said five will be in Canada, four in Europe, and one in Mexico.

“We continue to see significant opportunities for new warehouse growth, including new U.S. markets such as Buffalo, New York, and Lawrence, Kansas, infills in our more mature U.S. markets, as well as international markets in which we operate,” Vachris added during an earnings call.

There are 14 warehouses opening — 10 in the U.S. — across October and November, according to Costco. The retailer hasn’t shared store openings beyond that; it doesn’t comment on locations that are opening more than three months into the future, according to the New York Post .

Local reporting, however, shows Costco has been working to bring warehouses to places like Downey, California , which approved a plan for a new Costco earlier this year. Plans for warehouses in Charleston County, South Carolina , and Hillsborough County, Florida , were also submitted over the summer.

Efforts have also been underway in Fresno, California ; Lake St. Louis , Missouri; Southborough , Massachusetts; Silver Spring , Maryland; Scottsdale , Arizona; and Des Plaines , Illinois. The latter is anticipated to be a business center .

Costco has been experiencing a bit of a growth spurt this year , already opening stores in Arizona, California, Florida, Minnesota, New York, Texas, Utah, and Wisconsin (as well as Mexico and Taiwan).

Nexstar’s Alix Martichoux contributed to this report.
